record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Improve the current lower bound O(n / log^2 n) for the maximum possible obstacle number of an n-vertex graph.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 Improve the present lower bound O(n/ log2 n) of the obstacle number of a graph with n vertices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An obstacle representation of a simple graph $G=(V,E)$ in the Euclidean plane consists of an injective placement of the vertices $V$ as points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ together with a finite collection of pairwise disjoint connected closed sets ("obstacles") in $\mathbb{R}^2$, disjoint from the vertex points, such that for any two distinct vertices $u,v \in V$, the open straight-line segment $uv$ avoids every obstacle if and only if $uv \in E$. The obstacle number $\mathrm{obs}(G)$ is the minimum number of obstacles in any obstacle representation of $G$. Let
$$f(n) := \max\{\mathrm{obs}(G) : G \text{ is a graph on } n \text{ vertices}\}.$$
It is known that $f(n) = \Omega(n / \log^2 n)$. Improve this lower bound: that is, exhibit an explicit superlinear-in-the-denominator improvement, ideally proving $f(n) = \Omega(n/\log n)$, $f(n) = \Omega(n)$, or even a stronger lower bound, by constructing $n$-vertex graphs whose obstacle number grows faster than $n/\log^2 n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The lower bound has been improved several times since the problem was posed. Mukkamala, Pach, and Pálvölgyi (2012) gave Ω(n/log n) for general obstacles, and the bound for simple-polygon obstacles was improved to Ω(n/(log log n)^2) and subsequently (Balko, Chaplick, Ganian, Hliněný, Pach, Valtr, 2022) to Ω(n/log log n), with Ω(n) for convex-polygon obstacles. No matching Ω(n) bound is known for general or simple-polygon obstacles, so the question of the exact growth rate remains open.

status_evidence.title: Lower bounds on the obstacle number of graphs (Mukkamala, Pach, Pálvölgyi)
status_evidence.snippet: Improved lower bound Ω(n/log n) on the obstacle number of graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The original O(n/log^2 n) bound was improved to Ω(n/log n) shortly after the problem was posed.

status_evidence.title: Bounding and Computing Obstacle Numbers of Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: There are n-vertex graphs whose obstacle number is Ω(n/log log n) for simple polygon obstacles and Ω(n) for convex polygon obstacles.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent improvements give Ω(n/log log n) for simple-polygon obstacles and Ω(n) for convex-polygon obstacles.
